source.title: Diffused Redundancy in Pre-trained Representations
source.authors: Vedant Nanda; Till Speicher; John P. Dickerson; S. Feizi; Krishna P. Gummadi; Adrian Weller

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures redundancy in pretrained representations using random neuron subsets and downstream linear-probe performance. It does not test whether individual neuron poles have nameable jobs or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses neuron redundancy and polysemanticity in its background, but does not audit semantic jobs, validate neuron explanations, or assess attribution graphs. Its own results concern a related but different property: whether random subsets of neurons preserve representation similarity or downstream task performance. Table 1 reports this property; cited results from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper measures diffused redundancy (random neuron subsets retaining CKA similarity and linear-probe accuracy) in vision models. It never assigns or validates semantic jobs for neurons, never scores explanations, never revisits InceptionV1 neurons, and never builds attribution graphs. Polysemanticity is mentioned only in background citing Elhage et al. and Olah et al. Its results bear on no version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Authors conclude penultimate (and intermediate) layers show diffused redundancy, governed mainly by pretraining loss and dataset and by the downstream task, appearing only when layers are wide enough. They warn that dropping neurons concentrates accuracy losses on a few classes, a possible fairness-efficiency tradeoff.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures random-neuron-subset representation similarity and downstream linear-probe performance, rather than interpreting neuron poles or testing explanations against held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported redundancy varies with downstream dataset, pretraining loss and dataset, and layer width; the authors also report differences across architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Random subsets of penultimate-layer neurons in ImageNet-pretrained vision models keep near-full linear-probe accuracy. Diffused redundancy at delta=0.9 ranges 0.20 to 0.95 by model and dataset (Table 1). It is higher with adversarial training and ImageNet21k pretraining, shrinks with narrower layers, and is unaffected by dropout/DeCov.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained vision representations show diffused redundancy: random neuron subsets above a critical size retain near-full downstream performance, a property distinct from per-neuron semantic interpretability.

record.problems: The results concern downstream redundancy in pretrained vision representations, not semantic interpretability of neuron poles or validation of explanations. The paper describes DR estimates as approximations based on a few subset sizes and five random samples per subset size; the table does not give uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted as rows: the remaining figures and appendices report related redundancy measurements, but do not assess semantic jobs or any listed claim version.

untested.parts: All: no audit of neuron poles in Qwen3-32B or any language model.
All: no semantic-job shares in any language model, dense or MoE.
All: InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization are not examined.
All: dropout/DeCov results concern redundancy, not the share of interpretable neurons.
All: no attribution graphs or replacement models.
All: no neuron explanations tested against held-out activations.

record.verdict_notes: All 24 rows are correctly linked to 'none' with state cannot_determine, since the measure (downstream redundancy) cannot show any version's effect. The rows are this study's own Table 1 values, not selection values or cited results. The paper is not an original source. The relation is better described as cites_only/discusses: polysemanticity appears only in introduction and related work.

versions.untested_parts: The share of neuron poles with one or two nameable jobs and the share not understood; explanation testing on activations not used to write explanations.
Semantic-job shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or models up to trillions of parameters.
Whether the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron detects pose or reflects recursive generalization rather than superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain interpretability rates, including the stated InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
Whether attribution graphs using a model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict activation on new examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: ViT S-16
rows.operation_detail: Measured diffused redundancy from random neuron subsets using downstream linear-probe performance.
rows.measure: Diffused redundancy (fraction of neurons that can be discarded while achieving at least 90% of full-layer performance).
rows.note: This is a downstream-performance redundancy measure, not a measure of semantic interpretability.
